denial.premise_measurement: THE PRIOR RECORD'S PREMISE, RE-MEASURED AND REFUTED: attempt.init-item-info-data-declaration-lifetime-layout.20260829.v1 denies 'function-scope declaration and lifetime reordering' in prose with no scope, no measurement and no expiry check, and the natural reading of it is that declaration reordering is INERT on this function. It is not. Three `ninja -j2 build/GUNE5D/src/game/world/.postprocess/body/items.o` rebuilds scored with `wf_word_diff.py game/world/items InitItemInfoData`, each read back through the aligned view at 0x10c:0x158: HEAD 25 words at 106/106. (a) `s32 i;` moved from function scope into the enclosing block and `s32 overlay_offset;` hoisted the other way - 25 words, but the assignment MOVED and the two webs EXCHANGED registers exactly as intended: `@0x10c li r28,0` (i) became `@0x10c li r26,0` and `@0x110 li r26,0` (overlay_offset) became `@0x110 li r28,0`. Live axis, wrong distance: retail wants `@0x10c li r25,0` and `@0x110 li r30,0`. (b) on top of (a), `s32* node_slot;` hoisted out of the do-body into the enclosing block ahead of `i` - REGRESSED to 27 words, and the trade is exactly readable: node_slot reached retail's register (`@0x154 addi r26,r25,29816` against target `@0x154 addi r26,r27,29816`) while player_runtime left it (`@0x128 add r25,r30,r29` against target `@0x128 add r27,r31,r29`), so one web was bought and one sold. Within the enclosing block the LATER declaration takes the HIGHER register - node_slot declared first took r26 and i declared second took r27 - which is the fact that makes retail's {node_slot r26, i r25} unreachable from that block, because it needs i BELOW node_slot and there is no lower scope for i to live in.

hypothesis.statement: The whole 25-word gap is anchored by ONE web that no declaration lever reached: the materialised zero constant. Ours defines it at `@0x130 li r31,0` and keeps it in r31, the TOP of the callee-saved range, across four stores (`@0x138 stw r31,29864(r27)`, `@0x144 stw r31,29896(r5)`, `@0x184 stw r31,29848(r27)`, `@0x18c stw r31,29832(r27)`); retail defines the same web at `@0x130 li r28,0` and keeps it in r28, with r31 going to the sItemRuntime base instead (`@0x128 add r27,r31,r29` in target against `@0x128 add r27,r30,r29` in ours). Because the zero web sits above every declared local in our stream, `runtime` cannot reach r31 and everything below it is shifted, which is what produces five of the seven role mismatches. The web is COMPILER-GENERATED - it comes from four literal `= 0` stores in the source, not from any declared variable - so declaration order cannot rank it, and that is why probes (a) and (b) moved the leaves and never the root. The untried axis is to change how many stores share the zero: our four `= 0` stores are spread across the do-body at +0x74A8, +0x74C8, +0x7498 and +0x7488, and MWCC coalesced them into one long-lived web. Splitting them - for instance writing the two that bracket the MBOX_NewObject call as their own statements separated from the two that do not - would test whether the coalesced web is what earns r31, and it is the only lever left that touches the root rather than the leaves. It must be tried WITHOUT introducing a named zero local, which would be the contrived form AGENTS.md says to cap rather than commit.
